summary: A 1980 suggestion that systems install mail address synonyms for official roles, such as SYSTEMS or MANAGEMENT, so mail reaches whoever holds the job. It also suggests the NIC pick a standard set.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 763 suggests using stable mail aliases for official positions. The mail system could direct each role alias to whoever currently holds that position.

questions: how can mail aliases handle staff turnover
subtitle: A suggestion to use mail aliases for official roles rather than named individuals.

tldr.problem: Mail addressed to the holder of an official position can become undeliverable when that person leaves the role.
tldr.mechanism: The memo suggests mail address synonyms such as SYSTEMS, MANAGEMENT, and LIAISON that resolve to the current incumbent.
tldr.outcome: It recommends that systems support role synonyms and that the NIC or ARPANET management choose a common set.

today: RFC 763 is a brief suggestion for mail address synonyms for official positions. It proposes a standardized set but does not define one.

sections.title: Mail for an Official Position
sections.content:
The memo describes cases where a sender knows someone only as the incumbent of an official position. Employee turnover can make mail to the previous person's address undeliverable.

The author says NBS had encountered this issue and had created mail address synonyms for roles.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes a message needs to reach whoever holds a job, not one named person. A change in staff can otherwise make the old address fail.

sections.title: Role Mailbox Synonyms
sections.content:
The author gives SYSTEMS, MANAGEMENT, and LIAISON as examples of mail address synonyms. The system can use the synonym to deliver mail to the current holder of the role.

The memo suggests that systems permitting address synonyms install them.
sections.plainLanguage: A stable role name can point to the person currently responsible for that role. The memo gives SYSTEMS, MANAGEMENT, and LIAISON as examples.

sections.title: A Common Set of Names
sections.content:
The memo further suggests that the NIC or ARPANET management select a standardized set of role synonyms. The author argues that a common set would increase their usefulness.

The RFC offers this as a suggestion and does not define a required list or implementation procedure.
sections.plainLanguage: If sites used the same role names, those names could be more useful across the network. The memo does not define a mandatory set.
